reasoning_summary:
COMPLETE VERIFICATION, step by step (line numbers = the proof's numbered lines).

L0001-0250 (preamble, title, abstract, intro): LaTeX macros, authorship, abstract, and the defining equation (ck) for the k-point correlation function. No inferential content; the definition is the standard one. OK.

L0251-0257: sets up the induction target (moment33) E(X^[k]-X_*)^j <= (1+k/n^{2+eps/8j}) n^eps. Base case k=0 is (moment22); at k=2n^2 the prefactor is (1+2n^{-eps/8j}) so the bound is n^{eps+o(1)}, giving (moment11). Arithmetic checked, OK.
L0261-0268: truncation of the entries at log^B n. Overwhelming-probability events transfer between truncated and untruncated models; the moment perturbation is acknowledged and revisited at L0340. Justified.
L0271-0276: definition of D_k as the one-swap difference, conditioning on the common part M_0. Justified.
L0278-0283: for eta >= 1/n each resolvent diagonal entry is O(1/eta) <= n, so |s_xi| <= n; with T = n^{100} this gives |X^[k]| << n^{102} and the deterministic bound (moment00) |(X-X_*)^j - (X'-X_*)^j| << n^{102j}. OK.
L0288-0294: Proposition (Resolv) plus the Neumann-series Lemma (neum) and (xi-bound) transfer the (infty,1) resolvent bound from R_xi to R_0. Cited external inputs, internally consistent. OK.
L0296-0301: bad-M_0 contribution: probability <= n^{-102j-100} times the deterministic bound n^{102j} gives n^{-100}. Arithmetic correct.
L0303-0307: Proposition (proper) gives the cubic expansion (moment2) of s_xi with coefficients c_i(eta) << n^{o(1)}/(n eta) independent of xi. Cited; consistent.
L0309-0314: multiplying by n and integrating over eta in [1/n^{100}, n^{100}] gives (moment3) X_xi = X_0 + P(xi) + O(n^{-2+o(1)}), with d_i = n * integral c_i = O(n^{o(1)}) (the log factor is absorbed in n^{o(1)}), and |X_xi - X_0| <= n^{-1/2+o(1)} because |xi| <= n^{o(1)} a.s. OK.
L0316: trivial rearrangement of (moment3). OK.
L0318-0321: binomial expansion of (X_xi-X_*)^j. Terms containing P(xi)^m with m >= 4 are O(n^{-2+o(1)}) |X_0-X_*|^{j-m}, and the additive O(n^{-2+o(1)}) contributes j|X_0-X_*|^{j-1}n^{-2+o(1)}; the residual polynomial P_j has degree <= 3 in xi. The stated remainder sum_{l=1}^{j-1} is a (valid) over-estimate of the actual range l = 0..j-4, with the l=0 case absorbed by the n^{-5/2+o(1)} term since j > 5. OK.
L0326-0334: taking expectation in xi only; X_0 - X_* is deterministic once M_0 is fixed, so it passes through the expectation. OK.
L0337-0343: subtracting the xi and xi' versions; the first three moments of xi, xi' agree up to the truncation error, and the coefficients of P_j are only O(n^{O(1)}), so choosing the truncation constant B (hence C) large makes E(P_j(xi)-P_j(xi')) negligible. OK.
L0345-0349: replacing |X_0-X_*|^k by E|X_xi-X_*|^k. Justified because |X_0-X_*| <= E|X_xi-X_*| + n^{-1/2+o(1)} and Jensen gives E|X|^{1} <= (E|X|^k)^{1/k}; the residue n^{-k/2} is absorbed. (The internal reference should be to (moment8), not (moment0) - a citation typo only.)
L0351-0355: the two-case/Holder bound. If E|X_xi-X_*|^j >= n^{eps/2}, Holder gives sum_{k<j} (E|X|^j)^{k/j} <= E|X|^j n^{-eps/(2j)} <= E|X|^j n^{-eps/(4j)}; otherwise every term is <= n^{eps/2}. Correct.
L0357-0364: assembling with the bad-M_0 term gives D_k << n^{-100} + n^{-2-eps/4j} E|X_xi-X_*|^j + n^{-2+eps/2+o(1)}. Summing 2n^2 such increments against the induction hypothesis closes (moment33): the needed per-step budget is n^{eps-2-eps/8j}, and both 2 n^{eps} n^{-2-eps/4j} and n^{-2+eps/2+o(1)} fit inside it for large n. OK.

L0366-0374: appendix reductions for Proposition (ni): reduction to 1/n <= eta <= 1, dyadic rounding of eta, rounding of E to a multiple of eta, |E| <= n^{10}, union bounds, symmetry E >= 0. All standard and valid.
L0376-0381: diagonalisation in c, then argument by contradiction from (contra). OK.
L0382-0388: Im s(E+i eta) = (1/2n) sum eta/((lambda_j-E)^2+eta^2); each of the > n^{1+c} eta eigenvalues in [E-eta,E+eta] contributes >= 1/(2 eta), so Im s >> n^c. Correct.
L0389-0395: s = (1/2n) sum_j R_jj, so by pigeonhole some |R_jj| >> n^c; union bound over j. Correct.
L0397-0400: reduce to j = 2n by symmetry. OK.
L0401-0417: block expansion of W_{n,z} and of the minor W'_{n,z}, with X the removed column. Block sizes (n-1,1,n-1) sum to 2n-1 and the entries match the Hermitisation of (M_n-z)/sqrt(n); X = ((xi_{jn})/sqrt n, (xi_{nn}-z)/sqrt n, 0). Verified correct.
L0419-0424: Schur complement gives R_{2n,2n} = 1/(0 - E - i eta - Y_n) with Y_n = X^*(W'-E-i eta)^{-1}X. Correct.
L0425-0430: |R_{2n,2n}| >> n^c forces |E+i eta+Y_n| << n^{-c}; since Im Y_n >= 0 and eta > 0, Im Y_n << n^{-c}. Correct.
L0431-0435: SVD of the n x (n-1) matrix. OBJECTION (harmless): for an n x (n-1) matrix the vectors u_1..u_n in C^n are the LEFT singular vectors and the n-1 vectors in C^{n-1} are the RIGHT ones; the labels are interchanged. The conjugation of W' to a direct sum of 2x2 blocks plus one 0 block is correct.
L0437: the displayed inverse of the 1x1 zero block should be -1/(E+i eta), not +1/(E+i eta) (sign typo); moreover the corresponding term |X~^* u_n|^2 is silently dropped from the sum at L0440. Since that term is nonnegative and only an upper bound on the sum is used later, neither slip affects the argument.
L0439-0443: partial fractions w/(sigma^2-w^2) = (1/2) sum_{eps=+-1} 1/(eps sigma - w) verified, and Im 1/(eps sigma - E - i eta) = eta/((E-eps sigma)^2+eta^2). Correct.
L0445-0450: X~ is the top half of X. OK.
L0452-0453: Cauchy interlacing plus (contra) gives >> n^{1+c} eta indices with |sigma_j - E| <= eta; each contributes >= |X~^*u_j|^2/(4 eta), so Im Y_n << n^{-c} forces sum |X~^*u_j|^2 << n^{-c} eta. Correct.
L0454-0455: concentration of X~^* A X~ for the projection A onto those u_j; mean (j_+-j_-+1)/n + ||z pi(e_n)/sqrt n||^2 with Hanson-Wright-type fluctuation O(n^{-1+o(1)} ||A||_F) and cross term O(n^{-1/2+o(1)} ||z pi(e_n)/sqrt n||). Correct.
L0456-0458: AM-GM absorbs the cross term (a^2 - Ca >= -C^2/4 with C = n^{-1/2+o(1)}), leaving sum >> n^{1+c}eta/n = n^c eta, contradicting L0453. Correct; Proposition (ni) follows.

L0462-0466: R(i eta) = (W+i eta)(W^2+eta^2)^{-1}. Verified.
L0467-0470: W is block-off-diagonal and W^2+eta^2 block-diagonal, so W(W^2+eta^2)^{-1} has zero diagonal; hence R_jj and s(i eta) are purely imaginary with nonnegative imaginary part, and Im s = (eta/2n) tr(W^2+eta^2)^{-1}. OBJECTION (notational): the last expression should read (eta/n) tr((1/n)(M_n-z)^*(M_n-z)+eta^2)^{-1}; the 1/sqrt(n) normalisation of W_{n,z} is dropped here and in the later uses of sigma_j(M_n-z) and of A. This is a consistent abuse of notation, not a break in the argument.
L0472-0477: reduction to eta >= n^{-1+c}. The identity Im R_jj = eta sum_k |u_{k,j}|^2/(lambda_k^2+eta^2) (with the index typo lambda_i for lambda_k at L0473) plus monotonicity of eta^2/(lambda^2+eta^2), i.e. of eta Im R_jj(eta), transfers the bound to all eta > 0 with the loss n^{c+o(1)}(1+1/(n eta)). Correct.
L0478-0483: dyadic summation upgrades the bound to sum |u_{k,j}|^2/(lambda_k^2+eta^2)^{1/2}, and Cauchy-Schwarz gives the off-diagonal entries since |lambda_k - i eta| = (lambda_k^2+eta^2)^{1/2}. Correct.
L0485-0489: rounding eta to a power of two, trivial case eta >= n^{10}, reduction to i=j=2n and to the imaginary part. OK.
L0491-0496: with E=0, R_{2n,2n} = i/(eta + Im Y_n), so Im R_{2n,2n} = 1/(eta+Im Y_n). Correct.
L0497-0502: Im Y_n = eta X~^*(AA^*+eta^2)^{-1} X~ follows from the block structure ((W'-i eta)^{-1} restricted to the top block is i eta (AA^*+eta^2)^{-1}). Correct in substance (A must carry the 1/sqrt n; also the row vector is called Z at L0410 and Y here).
L0503-0507: crude bound Im R_{2n,2n} <= 1/eta since Im Y_n >= 0. Correct.
L0509-0513: concentration for the quadratic form with X~ = (zeta - z e_n)/sqrt n: mean (1/n)tr + (|z|^2/n) e_n^* (..) e_n plus the two error terms. Correct.
L0514-0517: ||B e_n|| <= ||B||^{1/2} (e_n^* B e_n)^{1/2} <= eta^{-1}(e_n^* B e_n)^{1/2}, then Young/AM-GM splits the cross term into o((|z|^2/n) e_n^* B e_n) + O(n^{-1+o(1)} eta^{-2}). Verified.
L0518-0523: ||(AA^*+eta^2)^{-1}||_F computed from the singular values; Proposition (ni) + interlacing give O(n^{o(1)}(1+nr)) singular values in [-r,r]; dyadic summation yields n^{1/2+o(1)} eta^{-3/2} = n^{o(1)}(n eta)^{1/2}/eta^2. Exponents checked, correct.
L0524-0533: interlacing gives tr(AA^*+eta^2)^{-1} = sum 1/(sigma_j(M_n-z)^2+eta^2) + O(1/eta^2) (one removed column changes the sum by at most one term), and (emo) converts it into Im s, giving (bbb). Correct up to writing s where Im s is meant (s is purely imaginary here).
L0535-0541: assembling: eta*(1/n)tr = Im s + O(1/(n eta)); eta * n^{-1+o(1)}||B||_F = n^{o(1)}/sqrt(n eta); eta * n^{-1+o(1)}eta^{-2} = n^{o(1)}/(n eta). Both are o(1) for eta >= n^{-1+c}. Verified.
L0543-0551: Schur complement for e_n^*(AA^*+eta^2)^{-1}e_n. Correct.
L0552-0555: the identity B^*(BB^*+eta^2)^{-1}B = 1 - eta^2(B^*B+eta^2)^{-1} is correct (from B^*(BB^*+eta^2) = (B^*B+eta^2)B^*), and substituting it turns the denominator into eta^2(1 + Y(..)^{-1}Y^*), giving eta e_n^*(..)e_n = 1/(eta + eta Y(..)^{-1}Y^*). Verified.
L0556-0563: concentration for eta Y (..)^{-1} Y^*; the Frobenius norms at L0560 and L0563 are missing the inverse (typo), but the stated bound n^{o(1)}(n eta)^{1/2}/eta^2 is the one for the inverse, so the intent is unambiguous.
L0564-0569: mimicking (bbb) gives eta e_n^*(AA^*+eta^2)^{-1}e_n = 1/(eta + Im s + o(1)) since (n eta)^{-1/2} = o(1). Correct.
L0570-0574: substituting into (roast-2) and (roast) gives (overwhelm). Correct.
L0576-0578: if |z|^2/n >= 1/2 then y + (|z|^2/n)/y >= 2 sqrt(|z|^2/n) >> 1 by AM-GM, so the denominator is >> 1 and (joe) holds. Correct.
L0580-0586: averaging (overwhelm) over the index gives the self-consistent equation for x = eta + Im s. Correct.
L0587-0590: the dichotomy x = o(1) or x + o(1) = (1+o(1))x, and in the latter case x = (1+o(1))x/(x^2+|z|^2/n) + eta. Correct.
L0591: dropping eta >= 0 and dividing by x > 0 forces x^2 + |z|^2/n >= 1+o(1); with |z|^2/n <= 1/2 this gives x >= 1/sqrt 2 - o(1) >= 1/2. Correct.
L0592-0595: the dichotomy is upgraded to all eta by n^{-100}-net + union bound + perturbation, and continuity plus the eta = n^{10} endpoint selects the second alternative throughout. Correct.
L0596-0600: hence Im s >> 1 for n^{-1+c} <= eta <= n^{-c}, so (overwhelm) gives Im R_{2n,2n} << 1; larger eta is covered by (crudito). Proposition (Resolv) follows. Correct.
L0602-0603: remark, no content to check.

L0605-0611: setup for Lemma (kernel); the error function is defined in the standard way, erf(z) = (2/sqrt pi) int_0^z e^{-t^2} dt. Note this definition, which fixes the normalisation used below.
L0613-0629: statement of Lemma (taylor). Parts (i),(ii) and the uniformity remark are fine; part (iii) asserts the value 1/2 + (1/2)erf(-sqrt 2 alpha). This constant is WRONG (see L0678): for z = n + alpha sqrt n the quantity is the Poisson(z) tail P(N <= n-1) -> Phi(-alpha) = 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-alpha/sqrt 2).
L0631-0635: case c > 1: the ratios |z|/j > 1+delta for j <= (1+eps)n make the terms exponentially increasing, so each term with j < n is <= e^{-kappa n} e^{|z|}; since |z| - Re z = O(1) = O(sqrt n) the factor e^{-z} converts this into O(e^{-delta n}). Correct.
L0636-0643: case c < 1: terms decay geometrically for j >= (1-eps)n, so the tail sum from n to infinity is O(e^{-kappa n}) after multiplying by e^{-z}, and the full series equals 1. Correct.
L0645: uniformity in a varying c: routine, correct.
L0647-0653: case c = 1: the argument of (i) shows the range j <= (1-eps)n is negligible, giving (sas) with a slowly growing window f(n) = o(n). Correct.
L0655-0658: Stirling j! = (1+o(1)) sqrt(2 pi n) j^j e^{-j} for j = n - o(n) (sqrt(2 pi j) = (1+o(1))sqrt(2 pi n)). Correct.
L0659-0662: the algebraic rewriting z^j j^{-j} e^{j-z} = exp(j(log(1+u) - u)) with u = (z-j)/j, and the Taylor bound j(log(1+u)-u) = -(1+o(1))(z-j)^2/(2j) = -(1+o(1))(n + alpha sqrt n - j)^2/(2n). Correct in the regime |z-j| = O(sqrt n).
L0663-0665: substitution of the last display into (sas). Correct.
L0666-0668: the tail of the sum beyond K sqrt n is declared O(eps). As printed the normalising factor 1/sqrt(2 pi n) has been dropped (the bare sum is of size ~ sqrt n e^{-K^2/2}); with the factor restored, as it is in the very next display, the claim is correct. Typographic slip only.
L0670-0676: the reduction to the window [n-K sqrt n, n), the substitution j = n + sqrt n t (so that the exponent becomes -(alpha-t)^2/2 and 1/sqrt(2 pi n) sum = 1/sqrt(2 pi) sum Delta t with Delta t = 1/sqrt n), and the passage to the Riemann integral (1/sqrt(2 pi)) int_{-K}^0 exp(-(alpha-t)^2/2) dt. All correct.
L0678: FIRST SUBSTANTIVE FAILURE. The asserted evaluation (1/sqrt(2 pi)) int_{-infinity}^0 exp(-(alpha - t)^2/2) dt = 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-sqrt 2 alpha) is false. Substituting s = alpha - t gives (1/sqrt(2 pi)) int_alpha^infinity e^{-s^2/2} ds = Phi(-alpha), and with the definition of erf at L0610 Phi(-alpha) = 1/2 + (1/2) erf(-alpha/sqrt 2). The two differ: at alpha = 1 the true value is 0.15866 while 1/2 + (1/2)erf(-sqrt 2) = 0.02275. The error is not cosmetic: it is exactly the constant that Lemma (taylor)(iii) and Corollary (iv) export, and it changes the resulting edge kernel (the corrected computation reproduces the known Ginibre edge density (1/2 pi) erfc(sqrt 2 u), whereas the printed constant gives (1/2 pi) erfc(2 sqrt 2 u)).
L0679-0680: dominated convergence / K -> infinity is a correct limiting argument, but it inherits the wrong constant from L0678.
L0682-0691: expansion of K_n(z_1 sqrt n + w_1, z_2 sqrt n + w_2) with z := z_1 conj(z_2) n + (z_1 conj(w_2) + w_1 conj(z_2)) sqrt n + w_1 conj(w_2). The identification of z (hence of alpha) is correct, but the printed Gaussian prefactors are wrong: expanding -|Z|^2/2-|W|^2/2+Z conj(W) gives exp(-n(|z_1|^2/2 + |z_2|^2/2 - z_1 conj(z_2))) and exp(-|w_1|^2/2 - |w_2|^2/2 + w_1 conj(w_2)), not the printed exp(-n(|z_1|^2-|z_2|^2+z_1 conj(z_2))) and exp(-|w_1|^2-|w_2|^2+w_1 conj(w_2)).
L0692: "the factor ... is trivial for z_1 = z_2 but decays exponentially for z_1 =/= z_2" is false for the expression as printed (it equals e^{-n|z_1|^2} when z_1 = z_2); it is true for the corrected factor exp(-n|z_1-z_2|^2/2). So L0686-0692 is internally inconsistent, and the corollary that follows uses the corrected halves.
L0694-0715: Corollary. Parts (i)-(iii) follow from Lemma (taylor)(i),(ii) and the (corrected) prefactors, and part (iii) does display the correct exp(-|w_1|^2/2-|w_2|^2/2+w_1 conj(w_2)) - which contradicts L0687. Part (iv) inherits the erroneous erf(-sqrt 2 (z_1 conj(w_2)+w_1 conj(z_2))) from L0626/L0678; the correct argument is -(z_1 conj(w_2)+w_1 conj(z_2))/sqrt 2.
L0717-0718: the phase factors e^{-i sqrt n Im(z_i conj(w_i))} occur in the conjugate-symmetric pattern phi(i) conj(phi(j)) and therefore cancel from the determinant. Correct.

L0720-0731: reduction of Lemma (corf) to the uniform bound K~_n = O(1), via the Pfaffian formula of Borodin-Sinclair and the antisymmetry (kt). Valid (a Pfaffian of a bounded matrix of bounded size is bounded).
L0733-0751: definitions of c_{n/2}, e_{n/2}, r_{n/2}, and the matrix kernel K~_n quoted from the reference. Quoted input; note the entry called ISM at L0748 is written IS in the case formulas (naming slip).
L0754-0775: the three cases of the kernel, quoted. No verification possible beyond internal consistency; consistent.
L0777: reduction to bounding each scalar entry. Valid.
L0779-0791: the r_{n/2} bound. Combining the quoted estimate with erfc(x) = O(e^{-x^2}/(1+x)) gives the factor e^{-|z|^2/2}, and the remaining ratio is (up to a factor |z|) a Taylor coefficient of e^{|z|^2/2}; since e^{-|z|^2/2} times the largest such coefficient is O(1/|z|), the conclusion r_{n/2} = O(1) does hold, although the printed factorial index ((n/2-1)! instead of ((n-1)/2)!) makes the one-line justification loose.
L0793-0800: |e_{n/2}(z)| <= exp(|z|) is immediate; the real-real bound for S~_n uses that -(x-x')^2/2 - x x' + |x x'| equals -(x-x')^2/2 (if x x' >= 0) or -(x+x')^2/2 (if x x' < 0). Verified, correct.
L0802-0806: the sentence "If one applies the same method ... one obtains" is left dangling (no display follows) - a text defect, not a mathematical one; the following bound |DS~_n| << |x-x'| exp(-(x-x')^2/2 - x x' + |x x'|) is correct.
L0807-0812: statement of the alternate bound |e_{n/2}(z)| << |z|^{1/2} exp(|z|)/| |z| - z |. Plausible and proved below.
L0814-0817: the identity (|z|-z)e_{n/2}(z) = sum_{m<=n/2} (z^m/m!)(|z|-m) - z^{n/2+1}/(n/2)! is verified by the index shift z * z^m/m! = m z^m/m! + boundary term.
L0818-0820: Stirling gives z^m/m! = O(exp(|z|)/|z|^{1/2}) uniformly in m, so the boundary term is O(|z| exp(|z|)/|z|^{1/2}) = O(|z|^{1/2} exp(|z|)). Correct.
L0821-0826: the two monotone pieces telescope (with b_m = x^m/(m-1)!) to 2 x^{M+1}/M! with M = floor(|z|), which is O(|z|^{1/2}e^{|z|}) by Stirling. Verified, correct.
L0829-0832: OBJECTION. Inserting the alternate bound for x x' < 0 gives, correctly, |DS~_n(x,x')| << (|x|+|x'|)/(|x||x'|)^{1/2} * exp(-(|x|-|x'|)^2/2); the display carries the exponential with the WRONG SIGN, exp(+(|x|-|x'|)^2/2), which is not O(1) and directly contradicts the next sentence. (With the corrected sign the claim still needs the min with the earlier bound to cover |x x'| <= 1, e.g. x = 1, x' -> 0, but then it is genuinely O(1).)
L0834-0838: reduction of the IS~_n bound to (clash) by symmetry, and the majorisation of c_{n/2} by cosh. Correct.
L0839-0840: OBJECTION. The stated closed form is wrong: substituting t = u^2/2 gives int_0^{(x')^2/2} e^{-t} t^{-1/2} cosh(x sqrt(2t)) dt = (sqrt pi/2) e^{x^2/2} [ erf((|x|+|x'|)/sqrt 2) + erf((|x'|-|x|)/sqrt 2) ], i.e. the prefactor is e^{x^2/2} (not e^{(x')^2/2}) and the two erf terms are added (not subtracted). The printed formula vanishes identically at x = 0, where the integral is sqrt(pi) erf(|x'|/sqrt 2) > 0.
L0841-0843: consequently the chain "<< exp((x')^2/2) exp(-max(|x'|-|x|,0)^2/2) <= exp(x^2/2)" also fails (take x = 1, x' = 10: the middle quantity is e^{9.5}, the right-hand one e^{0.5}). The target (clash) is nevertheless true, and follows immediately from the corrected closed form since the bracket is at most 2.
L0845-0849: complex-complex case. The modulus bound from (erfc-bound) and (enz) is correct, and the exponent rearrangement is verified: -Re((z-conj z')^2)/2 - (Im z)^2 - (Im z')^2 + |z||z'| - Re(z conj z') = -(|z|-|z'|)^2/2. Correct.
L0850-0855: the gain factor from the alternate lemma with w = z conj(z') is correct; the reduction to (fli) and the normalisations (|z|, |z'| comparable and > 1, Im z <= Im z') are legitimate.
L0857-0862: |conj(z') - z| << ||z|-|z'|| + Im z + |z| theta (from |e^{i phi} - e^{-i phi'}| <= 2 sin phi + O(theta)) and ||z||z'| - z conj(z')| = |z||z'| |1-e^{i theta}| >> |z|^2 theta. Both verified.
L0863-0865: the first two terms are handled (the Im z term uses Im z <= Im z' so that Im z/(1+Im z) <= 1) and the theta term uses the second entry of the minimum; the remaining cases are delegated to the reader. Correct.
L0867-0870: real-complex case. The exponent collapses to -(|x|-|z|)^2/2 (verified); the display writes (x-|z|)^2, which is only equal when x >= 0, but both are <= 0 in the exponent so the conclusion O(1) stands.
L0872: the sentence repeats S~_n(x,z) where S~_n(z,x) is meant, and the remaining bounds are left to the reader. Text slip; the delegated claims are plausible by the same method.
L0875-1066: bibliography and end matter; nothing to verify.

VERDICT: INVALID. The earliest failure that actually damages a conclusion is L0678 (the Gaussian-integral evaluation), which pushes a wrong constant into Lemma (taylor)(iii) at L0626 and into Corollary (iv) at L0710. Two further genuine errors occur later: the sign of the exponential at L0831 and the closed-form evaluation at L0839-0840 (with its consequence at L0842). Earlier slips (L0434 left/right singular vectors, L0437 missing minus sign, L0469 missing 1/n normalisation, L0473 index, L0529/L0532 s vs Im s, L0560/L0563 missing inverse, L0668 missing 1/sqrt(2 pi n), L0686-0692 missing halves and wrong sign in the prefactor) are typographic or notational and do not by themselves break the chain of reasoning, so they are not named as the flawed step.
